Exercise A

A Changing Wilderness

Read the text carefully, then answer the comprehension questions using the dropdown menus.

Reading Text

Canada is famous for its vast, wild landscapes: enormous forests, thousands of lakes, and the frozen Arctic in the far north. However, this beautiful environment has changed a great deal in recent decades, and not always for the better.

Climate change has hit the Canadian Arctic especially hard. Temperatures there have risen almost three times faster than the global average. As a result, the sea ice has become thinner, and many communities have had to change the way they live. Indigenous peoples, who have protected the land for thousands of years, have watched the ice they once relied on slowly disappear.

Canadians have not ignored these problems. In recent years, the government has created new national parks and has promised to cut greenhouse gases. Many young people have joined climate marches, and thousands of volunteers have planted trees and cleaned up rivers. Companies have started to use cleaner energy, such as wind and water power.

There is still a long way to go. Nevertheless, most Canadians agree that protecting their extraordinary natural environment is one of the most important challenges they have ever faced.

Exercise B

Present Perfect or Past Simple?

Use the present perfect for actions connected to now (with since, for, so far, recently) and the past simple for finished actions at a specific past time. The verb is in brackets.

Fill in the Gaps

1 Temperatures sharply in recent years. (rise)

2 In 2019, Canada a climate emergency. (declare)

3 Indigenous peoples the land for thousands of years. (protect)

4 The sea ice thinner since the 1980s. (become)

5 Last summer, wildfires huge areas of forest. (destroy)

6 Scientists the Arctic for many decades. (study)

7 So far, the government several new parks. (create)

8 Two years ago, she her first climate march. (join)
